name: Khasab Airport
before:
The airport for Khasab, the harbour town that is the capital of Oman's Musandam Governorate, on the Strait of Hormuz.

The setting is the story. The airport sits in a valley between two mountain ridges that come in close on both sides, and a third ridge stands just off the departure end of Runway 19, which carries a 270 metre displaced threshold as a result.
after:
The airport for Khasab, the coastal capital of the Musandam Governorate in Oman, on the Strait of Hormuz.

Its setting is the story: steep mountains come right down to the sea here, and the airport has a single runway.

The FCDO reports Iranian strikes and retaliatory attacks in Oman and elsewhere in the region since 8 July 2026 and tells British nationals in the Middle East to be prepared for flight cancellations and periodic airspace closures.

claims.note: Oman's own aeronautical information publication (eAIP issue of 3 September 2026) lists it as OOKB Khasab, south of Khasab City, administered by RAFO Khasab airbase.
Was 'the harbour town'. Only Wikipedia says harbour; the tourism ministry's page puts Khasab Castle on the coast of Khasab.

claims.note: Attributed statement, checked against the FCDO Oman page saved for this airport. Added in review (23 Sep), as for Salalah: Khasab faces Iran across the Strait of Hormuz. The FCDO names no area of Oman it advises against.
